html:
A merchant and banker of Augsburg in southern Germany, often called the richest man of his age. He lived from 1459 to 1525.

He took his family's cloth business into banking and mining. In return for loans to the Habsburg emperor Maximilian I, he got rights to the silver mines of the Tyrol, and with a partner he built a copper business in Hungary that supplied much of Europe.

His biggest deal was the election of 1519. The seven electors who chose the emperor expected bribes. Fugger lent most of the money that let Maximilian's grandson Charles V outbid Francis I of France. When Charles was slow to repay, Fugger wrote to remind him that without Fugger he would not have won.

He also founded the Fuggerei in Augsburg, housing for poor working families that still charges a symbolic rent. His bank funded the indulgence sales that Martin Luther attacked in 1517.
